text:
Longing for the sun on the rooftops,
on the dove-colored concrete wall
—so vivid nonetheless—and the sudden cold
that almost takes one's breath away.

The sweetness, the warmth of lips alone
in the middle of the familiar street,
like a great drawing room where distant crowds
might gather as though they were loved ones.

And above all the vertigo of time,
the great hole opening inward in the soul
while above it promises float,
fainting like foam.

This is surely the moment to think
that being alive demands something,
perhaps heroic deeds—or is it enough,
simply, to take some humble common thing,

its crust of earthly matter,
in one's fingers, with a little faith?
Words, for example.
Familiar words, worn warm by use.

translation.title: Poetic Art
